instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the whole wheat flour, rice flour, salt and cumin seeds together.
Gradually whisk in 3 cups of water until the batter is smooth and thin and pours like thin pancake batter. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, grate the carrot, and chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro and the curry leaves.
Stir the onion, carrot, cilantro and curry leaves into the batter. If it has thickened, add a splash of water.
Heat a large nonstick pan over medium-high heat until a drop of water sizzles on it.
Stir the batter, since the flour settles. Pour a scant 1/3 cup into the pan in a circle, starting at the outside and working in. Tilt the pan to fill any gaps.
Drizzle 1 tsp oil over the dosa. Lower the heat to medium and cook for 2 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp and the top looks dry. You don't need to flip it.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with the rest of the batter, stirring it each time. You should get about 10 dosas.
Serve hot with the coconut chutney.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen (the lead, 5 from 45) makes an instant batter of wheat and rice flour with no fermenting, so it's ready after a 10 minute rest. Its ratio is one third wheat flour to two thirds rice flour, which keeps the dosas crisp. Cook with Kushi's version is all whole wheat flour and gives a softer, thicker dosa, but has only 9 ratings. The green chili is left out of the base to keep it mild.
